title: Fixed edit budgets give exact bounds on equal-side synapse count scores
abstract: We ask how missed or extra synapses can change a bilateral count score on a fixed panel. For the mean of squared count difference divided by total count, we prove a sharp universal change bound of three times the edit budget divided by the number of pairs. A finite recurrence gives attainable bounds for each panel and local edit cap. In a synthetic 48-pair panel, 12 edits can raise the score from 0.625 to at least 1; a cap of two edits per pair requires 51 edits. Two omission patterns with the same 99.5 percent recall give scores of 0.050 and 10. We then use random gold-count audits to estimate the true fixed-panel score without assuming independent reconstruction errors. Local score bounds give a minimax audit allocation and a conservative finite-design interval. Exact enumeration checks the bounds and audit moments. In 27000 synthetic audit repeats, nominal 95 percent normal intervals cover only 86.8 to 94.8 percent; guaranteed cap-based intervals are too wide to decide the relation to 1. No real connectome was reanalysed. The results require fixed identities, a fixed equal-side reference and exact gold audits. They do not explain the measured fly excess or identify biological dispersion across animals. Original code, synthetic panels, attainable witnesses, results and proofs are supplied.

display.caption: Synthetic count bounds, equal-recall counterexample and exact audit-design standard deviations. No biological error rate is inferred.
